t: Carthage, a Phoenician colony of Tyre in Tunisia, built a trading empire across the western Mediterranean.
Its fleets, mercenary armies and Hannibal's invasion of Italy made it Rome's greatest rival for over a century.
Three Punic Wars stripped it of Sicily, Spain and its navy; Rome razed the city in 146 BCE and enslaved its survivors.
dyk: After destroying Carthage, the Roman Senate ordered the farming treatise of the Carthaginian writer Mago, in twenty-eight books, to be translated into Latin.
ev: Elissa (Dido) of Tyre traditionally founds Carthage
Carthage loses Sicily to Rome in the First Punic War
The Barcid family begins the conquest of southern Iberia
Hannibal crosses the Alps and invades Italy
Hannibal annihilates a Roman army at Cannae
Scipio Aemilianus storms and razes Carthage, ending the Third Punic War
